title: Classify by the highest derivatives.
caption: The first three classes allow successively more dependence on lower-order variables. In the last example the highest derivatives themselves enter nonlinearly. All displayed examples are second order.

title: Three evolution mechanisms.
caption: Dashed curves are initial profiles and solid curves are later profiles. Transport translates a shape; heat spreads a Gaussian while preserving its integral; the one-dimensional wave equation with zero initial velocity splits a profile into two half-amplitude translates. The panel axes are schematic and use separate scales.

title: High frequencies distinguish stability from solvability.
caption: For the Dirichlet mode $\sin(kx)$ on $(0,\pi)$, forward heat evolution multiplies amplitude by $e^{-k^2T}$; reconstruction multiplies by its reciprocal. Here $T=0.35$ and vertical scales differ. Arbitrarily small terminal errors in high modes can therefore give large reconstructed initial errors.

title: Loss of invertibility precedes a shock.
caption: For the local initial profile $g(\xi)=-\xi$, the characteristics meet at $t=1$. The characteristic formula is valid for $t<1$; the meeting point depicts failure of a classical continuation, rather than several values of an admissible solution at one point.

title: 连续依赖的方向
caption: 先说明数据与解各用什么范数，再检验解映射是否连续。存在、唯一和连续依赖是三个不同问题。

title: Read a transport solution backward.
caption: The solution is constant on each characteristic when the source is zero. With $b>0$, the forward line tilts right, while evaluation at a target requires its leftward initial foot $x-bt$. The orange arrow indicates evaluation backward in time, not a negative physical velocity.

title: A reflected point source enforces the boundary value.
caption: The solid source at $x$ is inside the upper half-space; the image at $x^*$ is outside and has the opposite sign. Every boundary point $y$ is equidistant from the pair, so their potentials cancel there. The labels indicate source signs, not signed coordinate locations.

title: A heat ball carries a nonuniform averaging measure.
caption: In one spatial dimension, fix a past time $\tau=t-s$. The blue band marks the allowed interval, while orange heights illustrate the factor $z^2/(4r\tau^2)$. The right panel shows its quadratic spatial dependence up to a fixed positive factor. This is a slice of the full space--time probability measure, not a separately normalized conditional density.

title: The wave equation has a finite domain of dependence.
caption: For speed one in one dimension, the solution at $(x,t)$ uses initial data only on $[x-t,x+t]$. At an intermediate time $s$, the relevant interval is $|y-x|\leq t-s$. In higher dimensions this interval becomes a ball. A forced equation also accumulates sources from the past cone.

title: 球体由球壳相加
caption: 先对每个半径做球面平均，再乘球壳体积并积分。体积平均的径向权重不是均匀的。

title: Noncharacteristic data permit local reconstruction.
caption: The projected characteristic direction is $F_p$. Transversality makes the initial-surface parameters together with the flow parameter independent local coordinates. A tangent direction makes this coordinate construction singular; it does not by itself prove that no solution can exist.

title: Legendre duality is a supporting-line construction.
caption: For $H(p)=p^2/2$ and $v=1$, maximizing $vp-H(p)$ finds the tangent point $p=1$. The tangent's intercept is $-L(1)=-1/2$. Convexity makes the whole graph lie above this line, which is exactly the Fenchel inequality.

title: Equal minimizing costs can produce a corner in the value.
caption: With $H(p)=p^2/2$, $t=1$ and $g(y)=\max(-|y|,-2)$, the Hopf--Lax cost at $x=0$ has two minimizers $y=\pm1$. Their candidate endpoint slopes $(x-y)/t$ differ. Indeed near $x=0$ the value is $u(x,1)=-1/2-|x|$, so it is not differentiable there.

title: Shock speed is a secant slope.
caption: For $f(u)=u^2/2$, the secant between $u_R=0.2$ and $u_L=1.4$ has slope $\sigma=0.8$. The tangent slopes satisfy $0.2<0.8<1.4$, so characteristics from both sides enter the shock. Reversing the spatial states keeps the secant slope but violates the compression direction.

title: 把路径在中途切开
caption: 中间点 $z$ 也要优化。两段代价相加后再取下确界，才得到动态规划恒等式。

title: A separated mode and its nodal line.
caption: On the unit square, this Dirichlet mode is the product of two one-dimensional modes. The dashed line $y=1/2$ is a zero set inside the domain. Applying $-\Delta$ adds the two eigenvalues, giving $5\pi^2$; heat evolution then changes only the time factor.

title: Fourier transformation turns differentiation into multiplication.
caption: The square commutes with the unitary normalization used here. There is no $2\pi$ in the multiplier because the exponential is $e^{-ix\cdot\xi}$. The heat multiplier is small at large $|\xi|$, connecting this representation with the stability picture in Chapter 1.

title: Radon data integrate along level hyperplanes.
caption: In dimension two the integration sets are lines perpendicular to $\omega$. The scalar $s$ is signed distance in the normal direction, not distance traveled along a line. The blue line is one member of the family; higher dimensions replace it by an $(n-1)$-plane.

title: Near a nondegenerate stationary point the scale is square-root.
caption: For phase $x^2$, oscillation is slow near its stationary point at zero and rapid farther away. The highlighted interval has width $2\sqrt{\varepsilon}$. Rescaling $x=\sqrt{\varepsilon}\,z$ explains the leading $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ factor in one dimension; cancellation, not pointwise smallness of the integrand, suppresses the outer region.

title: 一维有效系数
caption: 两个半格串联时通量相同，梯度与系数成反比。平均的是阻力 $1/a$，再取倒数。分段常系数可按弱形式理解。

title: A corner and a jump have different distributional derivatives.
caption: The continuous corner has a bounded weak first derivative. The step has a Dirac mass, so it has a distributional derivative but no weak first derivative representable by an $L^p$ function. The vertical Dirac arrow denotes mass, not a graph of a finite-valued function.

title: Reflection and zero extension treat the interface differently.
caption: Take $u(t)=1+t$ for $0<t<1$ and inspect only the interface at zero. Reflection matches values and preserves first-order Sobolev regularity locally. Zero extension inserts a jump and a Dirac mass in the first derivative. Even reflection still has a corner, so higher-order extensions need additional matching.

title: The dimension separates three embedding regimes.
caption: The diagram records standard continuous embeddings on a bounded $C^1$ domain with $n\geq2$. At $p=n$, the conclusion is valid for each finite $q$, with constants that may depend on $q$. It does not provide a uniform estimate as $q\to\infty$. Compactness is a further question addressed in the next section.

title: Bounded norms do not prevent concentration or escape.
caption: The left panel uses radial bump profiles $\psi(x)=(1-|x|^2)_+^2$ in $\R^3$, scaled with $\varepsilon=0.8,0.4,0.2$; their gradient $L^2$ and critical $L^6$ norms stay fixed. The right panel illustrates translations of a compact bump on $\R$. Each mechanism obstructs strong compactness for a different reason.

title: 沿法向控制边界值
caption: 先沿固定 $x'$ 的线段比较内部值与边界值，再对高度和切向变量积分。图中外法向朝下。

title: Ellipticity bounds the shape of the principal quadratic form.
caption: Here $\theta=1$ and $\Lambda=4$. The sublevel ellipse contains the circle of radius $\Lambda^{-1/2}$ and lies inside the circle of radius $\theta^{-1/2}$. A uniform positive lower bound prevents this principal geometry from degenerating as the base point varies.

title: Compatibility uses the adjoint kernel.
caption: In this explicit nonsymmetric matrix example, the range is the diagonal line. A right side with $f_1\ne f_2$ is unsolvable. Its obstruction is its component along $\ker M^T$, while the horizontal $\ker M$ describes nonuniqueness of solutions. The elliptic Fredholm alternative has the same distinction.

title: Localize before taking differences.
caption: The cutoff equals one on $V$ and is supported strictly inside $W$. A fixed geometric gap permits all sufficiently small positive and negative steps. The support condition is settled before the estimate; the estimate's constant must then stay independent of $h$ as $h\to0$.

title: Local positivity comparisons propagate along a chain.
caption: Choose overlapping balls whose slightly larger balls still lie inside $U$. Comparing at overlap points transfers a local Harnack bound from $x$ to $y$. The resulting constant depends on the finite chain and its distance from the boundary, which is why connected compact interior regions occur in the theorem.

title: 商为何在边界趋零
caption: 由 $|z|\leq Cd$ 与 $\phi\geq ad$，得到 $|z|/\phi^{1-\delta}\leq C'd^\delta\to0$。图示上界取 $\delta=1/2$。

title: Galerkin approximation preserves the energy estimate.
caption: The Dirichlet spectral projection is stable in $H^1_0$, controlling the time derivative in $H^{-1}$. Integrated tests retain the initial value in the limit. Arrows describe proof steps, not numerical error bounds.

title: The parabolic boundary and Harnack comparison.
caption: The thick bottom and side edges form $\Gamma_T$. The top interior belongs to the evolution region. Harnack compares an earlier interior slice to a later one; the arrow indicates forward propagation of positivity.

title: Anisotropy changes the cross-section of a wave cone.
caption: For $A=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)$, $q(x)=\sqrt{x_1^2/4+x_2^2}$. At time $t$, the dependency cross-section is an ellipse with semiaxes $2(t_0-t)$ and $t_0-t$. The cone sketch and the spatial slice use separate coordinate scales.

title: A Jordan block amplifies high frequencies.
caption: For $B=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and input $g=(0,\sin(kx))$ on a periodic line, $u=(-tk\cos(kx),\sin(kx))$. At $t=0.5$ the first component has amplitude $0.5k$. This exact periodic model illustrates the Fourier multiplier mechanism; the whole-space theorem above uses Sobolev data on $\R^n$.

title: 同一模态的两种衰减
caption: 热方程取 $E=\frac12\|u\|_2^2$，图示 $k=1$ 模态。波动方程取 $E=\frac12(\|u_t\|_2^2+\|u_x\|_2^2)$，同一模态总能量守恒。

title: The direct method keeps feasibility and energy in the limit.
caption: The arrows represent separate arguments. A finite-energy competitor makes the infimum meaningful; coercivity and Poincare give boundedness. Weak closure preserves constraints, while lower semicontinuity supplies the minimizing inequality.

title: Gradient oscillations test the need for convexity.
caption: The left graph is $W(p)=(p^2-1)^2$. A zero-trace triangular profile on $(0,1)$ can have slopes $+1,-1$ while its amplitude tends to zero. Its energy is zero, whereas the limit profile has energy $W(0)=1$. The right profile is one exact period, before multiplying its horizontal and vertical scales by $1/k$.

title: 秩一方向与全矩阵方向
caption: 对 $2\times2$ 矩阵，$t\mapsto\det(P+t\,a\otimes b)$ 是仿射函数，但 $t\mapsto\det(tI)=t^2$。秩一方向上的条件不等于整个矩阵空间中的凸性。

title: An exact obstacle solution with two free-boundary points.
caption: On $(-1,1)$ take $f=0$ and $h(x)=1-4x^2/3$. The minimizer is $u=h$ on $|x|\leq1/2$, and $u=4(1-|x|)/3$ outside. Values and first derivatives match at $\pm1/2$, so $-u''=8/3$ on the contact interval and zero elsewhere, with no point masses.

title: A minimax path must cross an energy barrier.
caption: This is an exact two-dimensional model, $I(x,y)=(x^2-1)^2+y^2-1$, connecting $(1,0)$ to $(-1,0)$. Both endpoints have energy $-1$ and every path crosses $x=0$, where $I\geq0$. The horizontal path attains maximum zero at the saddle $(0,0)$. Translation and addition of a constant put the first endpoint at the theorem's $0$ with energy zero.

title: Energy closes the weak-limit argument.
caption: The flux limit is initially named $\xi$. The Galerkin energy identity removes the weak--weak product; monotonicity with arbitrary $w$, followed by $w=u-tv$, identifies the weak equation. Each arrow requires its own justified limit.

title: Two ordered iterations trap the solution.
caption: For $-u''=1$ on $(0,1)$ with zero endpoint data, take $u_0=0$, $\overline u_0=x(1-x)$ and shift $\lambda=4$. The curves show the exact first lower and upper iterates and the solution $u=x(1-x)/2$. Later lower iterates increase and upper iterates decrease in the pointwise order.

title: 反应与扩散的阈值
caption: 归一化为 $\lambda_1=1$ 后，比较 ODE 为 $y'=y(y-1)$。箭头只表示这个 ODE 的相线；$y_0\leq1$ 时不能据此断言 PDE 全局存在。

title: Reflection and the region available for continuation.
caption: The cap $\Sigma_\lambda$ reflects inside the unit ball. At a proposed positive stopping position, comparison is uniformly strict on a compact core $K$. Any negative part for a nearby plane must lie in the thin remainder, where the small-support estimate excludes it. Geometry is schematic; the equation is scalar and $u>0$ is essential.

title: A nonsmooth energy can merge trajectories.
caption: For $H=\R$ and $I(s)=|s|$, $J_\lambda(s)=\operatorname{sgn}(s)(|s|-\lambda)_+$ and $S(t)s=\operatorname{sgn}(s)(|s|-t)_+$. The supporting slopes at zero form $[-1,1]$; different positive initial values reach zero at different times and thereafter coincide. These are exact graphs, not a discretization of another model.

title: A corner distinguishes a.e. and viscosity solutions.
caption: On $(-1,1)$ both $1-|x|$ and $|x|-1$ solve $|u'|=1$ away from zero and vanish at the endpoints. The upper test $1-x^2/2$ is allowed for the downward corner, with slope zero and residual $-1\leq0$. For the upward corner, the lower test $-1+x^2/2$ has the same residual and violates the required supersolution inequality. No smooth lower test exists at the downward corner.

title: Doubling variables produces two independent smooth tests.
caption: The common vector $(x-y)/\varepsilon$ need not be bounded. Global Lipschitz control in momentum handles the small difference $p_u-p_v$, while $|x-y|^2/\varepsilon\to0$ handles the spatial dependence of $H$. The opposite strict time shifts leave the positive gap $2\eta$ after subtraction.

title: A prefix and its continuation form one admissible control.
caption: Restricting a full control gives a continuation cost at least $V(z,t+h)$. Conversely, for a fixed prefix reaching $z$, choose one $\delta$-optimal continuation and concatenate it. The two comparisons prove the equality in DPP. The curves are schematic state trajectories, not a claim of optimality for the drawn paths.

title: 时间方向与测试符号
caption: 图中残差均按方程所写的时间变量计算。令 $\tau=T-t$ 后，$\partial_t=-\partial_\tau$，Hamiltonian 同时变为 $-H_c$；不能只改变时间端点而保留所有符号。

title: Two minimizing origins can create a viscosity corner.
caption: Take $H(p)=p^2/2$, $t=1/2$, and $g(y)=\min\{|y-1|,|y+1|,2\}$. The exact value is $\min\{h_t(|x-1|),h_t(|x+1|),2\}$, where $h_t(d)=d^2/(2t)$ for $d\leq t$ and $d-t/2$ otherwise. At $x=0$ the two minimizing origins are $y=\pm1/2$, both of cost $3/4$. The left panel shows $g$ and its value; the right panel shows the minimized cost at $x=0$.

title: Wave patterns in physical space
caption:
The left panel is a centered rarefaction: characteristic speeds increase
from $\lambda_l$ to $\lambda_r$. The middle panel shows a compressive
shock with $\lambda_r<\sigma<\lambda_l$; forward characteristics terminate
on it. The right panel is a contact, with equal characteristic and interface
speed. Only slopes and incidence are represented; these are schematic
panels for a single characteristic family.

title: 平均速度与压缩
caption:
本图取 Burgers 通量 $f(u)=u^2/2$、$u_l=1,u_r=0$。
激波速度恰为 $1/2$，两侧速度为 $1$ 和 $0$；
一般系统的平均公式只在小振幅下成立到二阶余项。

title: Matching states before placing waves
caption:
The endpoint map composes the family curves in state space. Its derivative
at zero consists of the independent eigenvectors. Disjoint speed intervals
then place those waves in increasing order in $x/t$. The unique small
strength vector is a local finite-dimensional conclusion; no general
system uniqueness theorem is inferred.

title: Compression reaches a vertical slope
caption:
An exact simple-wave example is the scalar Burgers characteristic map
$x=\alpha+t\,g(\alpha)$ for $g(\alpha)=-\alpha$ on a local interval.
Its Jacobian is $1-t$, and $u_x=-1/(1-t)$ until $t=1$.
The second panel plots this derivative. For two-field systems, the
weight in \eqref{eq:11-riccati} removes the mixed interaction and
recovers the same Riccati mechanism; the drawn map is the scalar model.

title: The entropy chord for a nonconvex flux
caption:
For $f(u)=u^3-u$, the chord from $u_l=-1$ to $u_*=1/2$ has slope
$-1/4=f'(1/2)$ and lies below $f$ on that interval. The entropy
solution for right state $1$ joins this shock to a rarefaction
$u=\sqrt{(x/t+1)/3}$ for $-1/4<x/t<2$.
A single jump from $-1$ to $1$ violates the chord criterion.
The exact states and speeds are derived in Problems 14--15.

title: The shrinking sections and the null flux
caption:
A spatial section of the backward unit-speed cone has radius $T-t$.
Energy leaves through the mantle with density
$\frac12|u_t\nu-Du|^2+F(u)$, measured using $dS/\sqrt2$.
The top section at $\tau<T$ is retained. The drawing is a one-space-dimensional
section of the $n$-dimensional cone, not a reduction of the PDE.

title: A complete ball for the weak-metric iteration
caption:
Every iterate stays in a bounded high Sobolev ball. Contraction is measured
in the lower energy norm; weak-star compactness identifies its limit with
the low-norm limit, preserving the high bound. The final linear equation
restores strong time continuity. The arrows describe a proof, not a
numerical convergence rate in the high norm.

title: 能量临界的缩放指数
caption:
图中 $a(p)=4/(p-1)-1$，且 $E[u_\lambda]=\lambda^{a(p)}E[u]$。
$p=5$ 是三维退聚焦波方程的能量临界指数；
它与后面聚焦小数据爆破的 $1+\sqrt2$ 阈值属于不同问题。

title: Why the cone must be enlarged
caption:
The flux tail first makes the potential energy small on shrinking cones.
Localized Strichartz and a linear Duhamel limit then exclude concentration
of the kinetic and gradient energy. At a fixed time $s$, the small-energy
ball can be enlarged by $\delta>0$. The enlarged sections retain a ball
of radius $\delta$ near $T$, allowing a finite cover of the fixed possible
support. A cone with zero terminal radius alone would not provide that cover.

title: Two different obstructions to a global solution
caption:
On the left, a positive concave quantity with negative derivative lies
below its tangent and must reach zero. The displayed curve
$J=1-t-t^2/4$ is only an exact concavity model, not a PDE solution.
On the right, $(p-1)^2<2$ leaves room for the positive $\varepsilon$
in the shell-based proof; the endpoint is excluded. Neither diagram
asserts a quantitative lifespan formula for the PDE.
